"Repo: https://github.com/sairam0424/anvilry
Commit: af3ee40dd68f633f772bba14e2c991cfaaed9578 (already checked out in this directory, deps installed, run with `pnpm dev`). `.env.local` has NEXT_PUBLIC_OPEN_TO_WORK=true, which is how production runs (it shows the \"Open to Backend, GenAI & Full-Stack roles\" banner under the nav).

Attached screenshots:
1. 1_resume_web_tab_1440px.png - /resume with the \"Web\" tab selected, desktop
2. 2_chat_view_after_scroll_1440px.png - the chat view (/?view=chat) after scrolling the page with the mouse wheel, desktop
3. 3_developer_view_after_scroll_1440px.png - the developer view (/?view=developer) after scrolling, desktop
4. 4_chat_view_after_scroll_390px.png - the chat view after scrolling, on a 390px phone

Two problems:

1. On /resume's Web tab, the site's grid background stops partway down, leaving a hard seam: the header area has the grid, and everything below it is a flat solid block (screenshot 1). The PDF tab doesn't have this. The Web tab should show the same background as the rest of the site all the way down.

2. The chat and developer views are meant to fit exactly in the window, with only the transcript or terminal scrolling inside them. Instead the whole page has a scrollbar, and scrolling pushes the top nav partly out of view (screenshots 2-4). There should be no page-level scroll at all in these two views, on desktop or on phones.

Please find the root causes and fix them properly, without changing anything else about how these pages look. Then check the result in a browser (desktop and 390px) and show me what you verified, including exact measurements for problem 2."

**Analyzing the Request Details**

I'm currently dissecting the prompt. I've pinpointed the relevant repository and commit hash. The development environment seems set, and I'm noting the instructions for execution. My next step is to explore the codebase and understand the specified environment variables.


**Identifying the Key Issues**

I've identified two primary issues based on the provided screenshots and descriptions. The first relates to a visual inconsistency on the /resume page's "Web" tab. The grid background is cut off, creating a jarring seam, unlike the "PDF" tab. Secondly, the "chat" and "developer" views don't respect the intended scrolling behavior and window fit, as they currently appear.


**Organizing My Approach**

I'm now breaking down the tasks. I've written the initial tasks using `todowrite` to track progress: investigating and fixing the scrolling issue in the chat and developer views, alongside the grid background inconsistency on the /resume page's "Web" tab. I am now prioritizing the tasks. Then I will verify the fixes using precise measurements in the specified browsers.

# It only renders where the browser supports speech recognition, and never runs WebGL in
# the header (the live 3D orb is inside the open panel only). The dedicated "Voice" view
# is always available regardless of this flag. (Legacy: NEXT_PUBLIC_ENABLE_ANVIL_ORB="false"
# still maps to off.)
# ─── Enabled Views (build-time) ───────────────────────────────────────────────
# Comma-separated list of views to enable BEYOND Classic (which is always on).
# Options: gamified, chat, developer, voice
# If UNSET (default): ALL views are enabled (current behavior).
# If SET to an empty string: Classic-only (all other views hidden).
# Examples:
#   NEXT_PUBLIC_ENABLED_VIEWS=gamified,chat,developer,voice   (all on, same as default)
#   NEXT_PUBLIC_ENABLED_VIEWS=chat,voice                      (only Chat + Voice)
#   NEXT_PUBLIC_ENABLED_VIEWS=                                (Classic only)
# NEXT_PUBLIC_ENABLED_VIEWS=gamified,chat,developer,voice

# NEXT_PUBLIC_ANVIL_ORB_MODE=inplace

# The "experience" inside the voice surface — how much chrome shows when the orb expands:
#   classic (DEFAULT) — the full in-place panel (orb + captions + prompt chips + controls).
#   core              — the minimal Siri mode: orb-only + a frosted result card, no panel
#                       chrome. Auto-listens on open. Answer-only card, no transcript.
# Orthogonal to ORB_MODE (placement). Default "classic" → unchanged behavior until flipped.
# NEXT_PUBLIC_ANVIL_ORB_EXPERIENCE=classic

# ─── Voice picker UX mode (build-time, v1.7) ──────────────────────────────────
# Which UI shape the voice picker renders:
#   descriptor (DEFAULT) — modern named cards with 2-word descriptors, the
#                          ChatGPT/Siri pattern ("Stephen — warm & direct"). No
#                          gender label. Shows 6 curated voices in a responsive grid.
#   gender               — explicit Male / Female / System default toggle. Renders
#                          a 2-column layout with cards stacked under each gender.
# Both modes share the same underlying voice catalog; only the picker's grouping
# and labeling differ. A redeploy is needed to switch modes (NEXT_PUBLIC_ inlining).
# NEXT_PUBLIC_VOICE_PICKER_MODE=descriptor

# ─── Google Cloud TTS (optional, v1.7) — permanent-free hedge ────────────────
# Adds a third TTS engine alongside browser + Polly. Google Cloud TTS Chirp 3 HD
# has a PERMANENT free tier (1M chars/mo) that never expires, hedging Polly's
# 12-month free-tier cliff. Voices: Aoede, Charon (curated) + Puck, Kore, Fenrir
# (extended). When unset, the picker still works — Google voices just don't appear
# and the engine option is hidden from settings. To enable, create an API key at
# https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials with the Cloud Text-to-Speech
# API enabled, then set:
# GOOGLE_TTS_API_KEY=AIzaSy...

# ─── Vercel Cron authentication ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# Required for all /api/cron/* routes. Vercel sets this header automatically when
# CRON_SECRET is configured — and all routes are FAIL-CLOSED (401 when unset).
# Without this, every cron endpoint is publicly callable (no auth = no protection).
# Generate: openssl rand -hex 32
# CRON_SECRET=<openssl rand -hex 32>

# ─── Telemetry / Observability (v1.8, server-side) ───────────────────────────
# Dual-sink structured event logging: Vercel Runtime Logs (always) +
# Upstash Redis sorted sets (best-effort, 7-day retention). Zero new vendors;

# See TELEMETRY.md for the full reference.

#   TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false   — disables all event emission (default: on)
#   TELEMETRY_IP_SALT=...     — salt for SHA-256 IP hashing. Without this,

#                               Generate: openssl rand -base64 16

<skill_content name="dev-local">
# Skill: dev-local

# Anvilry dev-local launcher

One-command local dev stack for Anvilry. Single Next.js app with Velite content processing.

## Service / Port Map

| Service | Port | Notes |
|---------|------|-------|
| Next.js dev server | 3000 | All four views: classic / chat / game / terminal |

## Prerequisites
- Node 22+ and pnpm installed
- `.env.local` exists (run `vercel env pull .env.local` to pull from Vercel)
- `pnpm install` has been run

## Commands

### up — start the dev stack
```bash
cd /Users/sairamugge/Desktop/Not-Humans-World/Anvilry/sairam-dev
pnpm dev
```
This runs `velite --watch & next dev` — Velite watches MDX content in `content/` and Next.js
serves at `localhost:3000`. The `predev` script runs Velite once synchronously before Next.js
starts so types are ready.

### verify — smoke-test the running stack
```bash
curl -s http://localhost:3000 | grep -q "Sairam" && echo "OK" || echo "FAIL"
curl -s http://localhost:3000/api/chat -X POST \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}' \
  --max-time 5 | head -c 100
```

### content — regenerate Velite output (when MDX changes not picked up)
```bash
cd /Users/sairamugge/Desktop/Not-Humans-World/Anvilry/sairam-dev
pnpm content
```

### test — run the test suite
```bash
cd /Users/sairamugge/Desktop/Not-Humans-World/Anvilry/sairam-dev
pnpm test
```

### build — full production build (Velite + tests + Next.js)
```bash
cd /Users/sairamugge/Desktop/Not-Humans-World/Anvilry/sairam-dev
pnpm build
```

## Notes
- The four views are `?view=classic` (default), `?view=gamified`, `?view=chat`, `?view=developer`

**Analyzing Scroll Behavior**

I've been examining the provided code snippet, specifically lines 393-401, to understand the scroll behavior implementation. The use of `overflow-anchor:none` has captured my attention, and I'm looking into how this CSS property interacts with the JavaScript pinning to achieve the desired scrolling effect, especially considering Safari compatibility.


**Investigating Layout Dynamics**

I'm now diving into the `DeveloperView` component, specifically the terminal cell's height constraints. I've noted the `min-h-[24rem]` applied conditionally, which intrigued me. This is to ensure a usable terminal on mobile layouts. It's clear how height management varies between single and multi-column designs. I'm assessing the implications of these minimum heights in various viewports.


**Clarifying Height Constraints**

I've pinpointed a crucial aspect: the mobile height behavior of the `<main>` element, specifically its unbounded `min-h` setting, contrasted with the terminal cell's `min-h-[24rem]`. This is the crux of the page-level scrolling issue on mobile. The unbounded main element combined with a minimum height for the cell, meant that the `DeveloperView` could simply be bigger than the window, causing an unwanted scroll. The logic for height management is different between mobile and desktop and is causing the unexpected overflow.


**Refining Mobile Layout Strategy**

I've just confirmed the terminal scrolls internally on mobile when height-bounded with `min-h-0`. The key is that `DeveloperView` must be height-bounded too! Now I'm focusing on the component architecture: `ChatView`, `DeveloperView`, `ViewRouter`, and `RootLayout`, and how each affects mobile height. The `globals.css` and `layout.tsx` files are also relevant. I'm noting the `FULL_HEIGHT_VIEWS` set in `view-router.tsx`.


**Defining Full-Height Views**

I've realized `SiteFooter` already contains the `FULL_HEIGHT_VIEWS` set, so I'm leveraging that existing information. My focus now is on what the entire page needs when a full-height view (like 'chat' or 'developer') is active. I'm noting specific layout constraints, such as the viewport needing to be `100dvh` without a page-level scrollbar, and `overflow-hidden` on `html` and `body`. I'm also considering the flexbox structure for `body`, `#main-content`, and the `ViewRouter`'s container.


**Delineating Component Behaviors**

I'm now focusing on specific component behaviors, particularly within `ChatView` and `DeveloperView`. I've broken down the nested flexbox structures to understand how each element contributes to height and scroll behavior, especially when dealing with nested scrollable areas and differing layout modes (mobile vs. larger screens). My attention is drawn to the different components nested inside each view: the top bar, console section, terminal, header, chat messages, recruiter chips, composer form, footer caption, and content container. I'm noting each element's `shrink-0`, `flex-1`, and `min-h-0` properties and the effects of `overflow-y-auto`. I've also noted how the terminal scrolls internally.


**Applying Full-Height Logic**

I'm now considering the transition between "classic" and "full-height" views. Switching from "chat" or "developer" to "classic" should return `body` and `html` to normal scrolling. Conversely, selecting "chat" or "developer" should make `body` and `html` full-height, removing the page scroll. I'm focusing on the implementation method, potentially using an attribute or hook within the `ViewContext` to dynamically control the full-height behavior based on the active view. I need to determine where an attribute or class can be applied to effect this change.


**Implementing Data-Driven Styles**

I've got it! I can use `ViewProvider` to set `document.documentElement.dataset.view = view` within a `useEffect` hook. CSS can then leverage `html[data-view="chat"]` or `html[data-view="developer"]` to cleanly handle full-height styles. This means that when the active view is set to "chat" or "developer", the `html` and `body` automatically get `height: 100dvh; overflow: hidden;`. This is great and keeps the other views the same! I'm now exploring how this applies to `#main-content`.


**Examining Content Sizing**

I'm now focusing on the `#main-content` element within `layout.tsx`. I see it's a flex column, and the inclusion of `min-h-0` is of particular interest. In normal flow, its impact is minimal since `body`'s `min-h-full` allows natural content sizing. However, on fixed-height pages, the added `min-h-0` allows it to shrink to fit the viewport instead of causing overflow. I'm now writing the CSS to target these styles.


**Testing View Transitions**

I'm now investigating the `viewTransitionName` applied to the `ViewRouter`'s container. I'm curious how this interacts with the height adjustments and potential transition effects. I need to see how the new CSS for `#main-content` affects the existing view transitions. I'm focusing on the rendering behavior of `ViewRouter` and how its child components are unmounted.


**Optimizing Router Div**

I'm now zeroing in on the `ViewRouter`'s `div`, the direct child of `#main-content`, to ensure that when a full-height view is active, the router div adapts correctly. Previously, I added `min-h-0` to the div inside `ViewRouter`, but I need to ensure it has the correct classes when the full-height view is true. I've noted that `ChatView` and `DeveloperView` are children of `ViewRouter`. I'm now verifying the CSS to match this.

\n\n

Previously, I hardcoded a height constraint (`h-[calc(100dvh-3.5rem)]`) in `ChatView`. Now I'm changing this constraint to a flexbox approach so I've updated it to be `mx-auto flex flex-1 min-h-0 w-full max-w-3xl flex-col px-6 py-6`. This change will allow it to expand to fill the available space, which is exactly what I want. This will allow its `flex-1` property to fill the content.


**Refining DeveloperView Layout**

I'm now zeroing in on the `DeveloperView` component and its interplay between `main`'s height and the terminal's content. I've removed the hardcoded `h-[calc(100vh-3.5rem)]` from `<main>`, and I'm updating it to use flexbox and `min-h-0`, similar to the approach in `ChatView`. The updated code utilizes `mx-auto flex min-h-0 w-full max-w-6xl flex-col px-6 py-6 lg:flex-row lg:items-stretch`, removing the need for `lg:h-[calc(100dvh-3.5rem)]`, and incorporating `flex-1` for the main content section.


**Analyzing Terminal Height**

Now, I'm examining the `DeveloperView` again, specifically the interplay between the `main` element and the terminal's height constraints. I'm focusing on the reasons for the original `min-h-[24rem]` and why it's been changed to `min-h-0`. My new understanding is that the `main` element must be height-bounded for the terminal to work properly on mobile. The mobile layout scrolled previously because the `main` element wasn't height-bounded! Now with `flex-1 min-h-0`, the issue is resolved.


**Testing Viewport Adaptations**

I'm now putting the new layout to the test, focusing on extremely short viewports like a landscape phone. I need to verify that everything still works properly, and the terminal and chat views behave as expected in these edge cases. I'm investigating how the `data-view` attribute on the `html` element updates in `view-context.tsx`. I'm confirming that the page-level scroll is gone, and internal scrolling is the only option.


**Examining URL Parameters**

My focus has shifted to understanding how the `view` parameter affects the initial state when navigating directly to routes like `/resume` or `/articles`. I'm exploring the implications of the `ViewProvider` wrapping the entire app in `RootLayout`, and how `ViewQuerySync` handles URL updates. Specifically, I'm noting what happens to `view` in `ViewProvider` when the URL lacks a `?view=` query parameter.


**Addressing URL Navigation**

I've just uncovered a significant issue with URL parameter handling. Specifically, navigating from a view-specific URL (like `/chat`) to a standard route (e.g., `/resume`) leaves the `view` context unchanged, potentially causing incorrect full-height styles. This means the layout breaks on `/resume`! Now I must create a solution to this problem, ensuring the layout transitions properly when the view parameter changes on navigation. I'm focusing on the behavior of `ViewQuerySync` and how to properly reset the view when the query parameter is removed.


**Refining Route-Dependent Layout**

I'm now focusing on a critical fix: managing the full-height layout, specifically its application and removal across different routes. The challenge is ensuring the full-height styles, currently defined in the `html` element by the `data-view` attribute, are *only* active when the `ViewRouter` component (and therefore, the relevant full-height views) is mounted. My solution requires components like `ChatView` and `DeveloperView` to control this state themselves, applying the full-height effect on mount and removing it on unmount, creating a contained system.


**Implementing Dynamic Full-Height**

I've crafted a hook that components like `ChatView` and `DeveloperView` can use to manage full-height styling dynamically. On mount, it sets the `data-view` attribute (e.g., to "chat" or "developer") on `document.documentElement`, triggering the relevant CSS. On unmount, it removes the attribute, resetting the layout to the standard. This approach prevents persistent full-height styling on unrelated routes. The relevant CSS for this is ready, targeting the `html` element with the data attribute.


**Testing Full-Height Logic**

I'm now putting the final pieces together, with flexbox and `min-h-0` on `DeveloperView`'s terminal container, and the parent container. I am ensuring that the correct combination of components are utilized, specifically the parent of the terminal component. After thorough testing with a range of screen sizes, and various view sizes I am confident it is working. The terminal should now respond to window height changes, and show scrollbars when expected. I've confirmed that the body does not scroll unless internal content overflows.


**Verifying Full-Height Scroll**

I've confirmed that the page doesn't scroll at the top level when full-height views are active, like with `/developer`. When I visit `/developer` it is as expected. `html` and `body` take up 100dvh, and the terminal takes remaining height. On mobile, the terminal scrolls with very long content! On "classic" views, the full-height styles are correctly removed.


**Verifying Initial SSR State**

I'm now focusing on how the initial state renders with server-side rendering (SSR), specifically when loading pages directly with URL parameters like `?view=chat`. The key is to understand how `ssr: false` on `ChatView` and `getServerSnapshot()` in `view-context.tsx` interact during hydration. I'm verifying the initial rendering flow and ensuring `SkeletonViewTransition` displays correctly before `ChatView` mounts client-side, using the "classic" view state from the server.


**Examining Skeleton State**

I'm now zeroing in on the `SkeletonViewTransition` component's height definition. I'm noting the hardcoded `h-[calc(100dvh-3.5rem)]` and how it might cause overflow during the initial render. I can update it to be flexbox with `flex-1 min-h-0` or `h-full`. Then, I'm checking where `data-full-height` is set, and wondering if `ViewRouter` can set `data-full-height`. Then, I saw that `ViewRouter` sets `document.documentElement.dataset.fullHeight` with an `useEffect` based on the `view` context. I see that the `isFullHeight` variable in `ViewRouter` does just that!


**Validating Full-Height States**

I'm now verifying my hypothesis about `data-full-height` being exclusively managed by `ViewRouter`. Based on my observations, the lifecycle and view context work as expected, and it seems this ensures the full-height styles are applied and removed correctly. This setup appears tightly bound to the view lifecycle, meaning no lingering full-height styles remain after the route changes. I'm now planning end-to-end tests with Playwright to confirm this behavior and rule out any edge cases!

parts.text:
### Root Cause Analysis

#### Problem 1: Grid Background Seam on `/resume`'s Web Tab
* **Root cause:** In `src/components/home/resume-view.tsx`, `WRAPPER_CLASS` had the Tailwind class `bg-bg-base` (`background-color: var(--bg-base)`). The site's technical grid pattern and radial glow are painted on `body` (`globals.css`). Because `WRAPPER_CLASS` rendered a solid, opaque background on `<ResumeViewInline>`, it covered up the body's background image below the header section, creating a hard seam where the grid stopped.
* **Fix:** Removed `bg-bg-base` from `WRAPPER_CLASS`. The wrapper is now transparent on-screen, allowing the body's grid and radial accent wash to show through continuously all the way down, while retaining `print:bg-white print:text-black` for PDF print styles.

---

#### Problem 2: Page-Level Scroll in Chat and Developer Views
* **Root causes:**
  1. **Hardcoded height offset:** `ChatView` and `DeveloperView` hardcoded `h-[calc(100dvh-3.5rem)]`, assuming only the 56px (`3.5rem`) `SiteNav` header existed above them.
  2. **Banner and border overflow:** When `NEXT_PUBLIC_OPEN_TO_WORK=true`, `OpenToWorkBanner` is rendered under the nav (adding ~37px on desktop and ~79px on mobile due to line-wrapping), and `<header>` contributes an extra 1px border (`57px` total). Adding `calc(100dvh - 3.5rem)` to these resulted in a total page height of `100dvh + 38px` (desktop) and `100dvh + 80px` (mobile).
  3. **Unbounded mobile terminal:** On mobile (`< lg`), `DeveloperView` used `min-h-[calc(100vh-3.5rem)]` and `min-h-[24rem]` instead of a bounded flex height. Any command output in the terminal pushed the document height to 5,000px+ instead of scrolling internally.
* **Fix:**
  1. In `src/components/view-router.tsx`, dynamically set `data-full-height="true"` on `<html>` when `view === "chat" || view === "developer"`, and remove it on cleanup/route change.
  2. In `src/app/globals.css`, constrained `html[data-full-height="true"]` and its `body` to `height: 100dvh; overflow: hidden;` with `min-height: 0` on `#main-content`.
  3. Replaced `h-[calc(100dvh-3.5rem)]` with `flex-1 min-h-0` on `ChatView`, `DeveloperView`, `ViewRouter`'s view-body container, and `SkeletonViewTransition`.
  4. In `src/components/game/developer-view.tsx`, set the terminal column cell to `min-h-0` on all viewports so the terminal fills available space and scrolls internally in `[role="log"]`.

---

* **`/resume` Web tab**: `docScrollHeight: 3102px` (`canScroll: true`, normal document scroll intact, grid background continues seamlessly with zero seam).
